meta.purpose: Accepted validation standards, reasonableness ranges, elasticities and real-model benchmarks for validating a San Francisco trip-based model (nested logit mode choice, optimal-strategies transit assignment).
meta.rule: Every number below was read from the cited document as fetched (text extracted from the PDF/HTML). Page numbers are the printed page numbers unless marked pdfPage. Where a table could not be read as text (chart or image), it is listed under notFound instead of guessed.
meta.caveat: Every guidance document here says that its thresholds are guidelines, not pass/fail standards (FHWA 2010 §9.1.4 and §9.2.4; TAG M3.1 §3.2.2; CTC: 'MPOs are encouraged to meet...').

vmtByFunctionalClass.table: Table 9.2 Example VMT Guidelines by Functional Class and Area Type (p. 9-19)

vmtByFunctionalClass.note: The extracted text lines up the columns as shown. Check the PDF table before quoting a single cell.

pctRmseByVolumeGroup.value: Figure 9.8 plots target %RMSE against link-volume group for Florida (acceptable and desirable), Ohio and Oregon. It is a chart, so no numbers are printed. The Florida values in table form are in other.floridaFsutms2008.pctRmseByVolumeGroup.

screenlines.value: Michigan DOT targets: 5% for screenlines and 10% for cutlines (percent difference, observed vs estimated)

Figure 9.9 shows the maximum desirable deviation in total screenline volume against screenline volume (from FHWA 1990 'Calibration and Adjustment of System Planning Models'). It is a chart, so no numbers are printed.

geh.value: The GEH statistic is not mentioned anywhere in the FHWA 2010 manual (searched the full text). For GEH, use UK TAG M3.1 (other.ukTag.m31).

sensitivity.test: Regional: multiply all trips (e.g. ×1.5). VMT should change by a similar factor, or by more where congestion is heavy
Localized: remove a key bridge or facility, reassign a fixed trip table, review volume-difference plots
Over-sensitivity: a minor change (e.g. one lane on a minor arterial) should have only very local effects

floridaTransitGuideline.table: Table 9.9 Example Transit Assignment Validation Guideline for State of Florida (p. 9-32), from FSUTMS-Cube Framework Phase II (Cambridge Systematics for FDOT, 2007-12-31)

pmt.value: Transit PMT is analogous to VMT, so a regional VMT guideline (e.g. ±5%) may be applied to modeled vs observed PMT

fta.value: FTA sets no numeric guidelines for New Starts; the modeling should 'tell a coherent story'

stringency.value: Use a 'tight' validation when assigning an observed (on-board survey) trip table. Less stringent criteria are appropriate when assigning modeled trip tables, because the test then covers the whole model chain

exampleResults.value: system total modeled 432,497 vs observed 441,385 daily boardings (-2%); operators -19% to +21%
all screenlines -26% (193,564 modeled vs 261,025 observed); individual screenlines -73% to +44%
total boardings ratio 1.00 (92,760 vs 92,418); LRT 0.90; RT bus 1.01

reasonableness.value: typically 1.2 to 1.6; higher in regions with grid bus systems and fixed-guideway modes
radial lines: near the CBD or major generator; crosstown lines: near the middle of the route
boardings per linked trip and PMT per linked trip should stay roughly constant from base to future unless the system changes

sensitivity.test: Regional: multiply trips (e.g. ×1.5). Total boardings should change by a similar factor
Localized: change speeds or headways on selected routes. Faster or more frequent routes should attract riders; removing a route should shift riders to others
Mode: add a known number of linked rail trips. Rail boardings should rise by at least that number

criteria.value: No specific criteria guidelines for trip generation

nhts2001TripRatesPerHousehold_MSAover3M.table: Table 5.2 (by persons), 2001 NHTS, MSA population > 3 million, all-households column (p. 5-10). Rates include motorized and nonmotorized trips

tripGeneration.note: FHWA says sensitivity testing of aggregate trip generation is 'not considered to be very useful'

criteria.value: modeled within 5% of observed (can be relaxed for purposes with few trips)
within 3 percentage points of observed for each purpose (used by some models)

sensitivity.value: Elasticities of travel with respect to level of service are 'generally well below 1.0 in absolute value'. Suggested tests: change speeds, CBD parking cost, tolls, transit times/headways/fares by a fixed percentage

criteria.value: No applicable criteria guidelines. Matching base-year shares by market segment is desirable, but the 'observed' shares are themselves assembled from several data sources

parameterReasonableness.value: about 2 to 3 for HBW, with higher values for nonwork

parameterReasonableness.measure: Value of in-vehicle time (model base-year $, not normalized)

parameterReasonableness.value: -0.02 to -0.03 per minute ('some further analysis' if outside this range)
approximately equal to the HBW IVT coefficient
2 to 3 × the IVT coefficient ('compelling evidence' needed outside this range)
must be between 0 and 1 (and statistically different from both if estimated); a lower nest's coefficient must be below its parent's
IVT -0.025, auto OVT -0.050, transit walk/wait/transfer -0.050 per min

elasticities.value: Transit demand elasticities with respect to level-of-service variables are 'usually well under 1.0 in absolute value'
Simpson-Curtin rule: fare elasticity of transit demand is about -0.3
Arc elasticity formula: (ln q2 - ln q1)/(ln p2 - ln p1) (Eq. 7.2)

sensitivityTests.value: Change highway or transit times regionwide by a fixed percentage; CBD parking cost; headways on selected routes or submodes; fares on selected submodes; shift development patterns; reallocate households by income

rows.metric: Percent of links with volume-to-count ratio within the Caltrans deviation allowance

staticValidationThresholds.source: ctc2017 'Recommended Static Validation Thresholds' p. 49 (pdfPage 60); repeated unchanged in ctc2024 p. 55

rows.metric: Actual counts vs model results, by route group (e.g. local bus, express bus)
Actual counts vs model results, by transit mode (e.g. light rail, bus)

transitAssignmentThresholds.source: ctc2017 'Recommended Transit Assignment Validation Thresholds' p. 49; repeated unchanged in ctc2024 p. 55

definitions.value: Volume-to-count ratio = model volume / count. The Caltrans deviation allowance shrinks as the count grows. Correlation coefficient between counts and model volumes. %RMSE as defined by FHWA

speeds.value: Because emissions are sensitive to speed, US EPA and US DOT suggest comparing modeled validation-year speeds with observed peak and off-peak speeds

nonCompliance.value: 'MPOs are encouraged to meet the recommended ... thresholds ... Where a model does not meet the thresholds, the MPO is encouraged to clearly document impediments.'

pctErrorByFunctionalClass.definition: total assigned volume / total counted volume for counted links, by functional class
pctErrorByFunctionalClass.source: caltrans1992 §3.5.3 p. 65-66 (citing FHWA, Calibration & Adjustment of System Planning Models, Dec 1990)

linkSpecific.value: 75% of freeway and principal arterial links, and all screenlines, within the maximum desirable deviation of Figure 3-9

countCoverage.value: aim for counts on 10% or more of region-wide highway segments (and in each functional class)

transit.value: Calibrate and validate transit assignment the same way as highway assignment, with ridership counts in place of traffic counts. No numeric transit thresholds are given

status.value: 'The last Caltrans travel forecasting guidance, published in November 1992...' No Caltrans 2014 Travel Forecasting Guidelines were found

screenlines.criterion: modeled vs counted flow difference < 5% of counts

criteria: Individual flows within 100 veh/h of counts for flows < 700 veh/h: more than 85% of cases
Within 15% of counts for flows 700-2,700 veh/h: more than 85% of cases
Within 400 veh/h of counts for flows > 2,700 veh/h: more than 85% of cases
GEH < 5 for individual flows: more than 85% of cases
linkFlows.gehDefinition: GEH = sqrt(2(M-C)^2/(M+C)), where M = modeled hourly flow and C = observed hourly flow. In the PDF the equation is an image; M and C are defined in the text. The flow and GEH criteria are 'broadly consistent' and a flow meeting either is satisfactory

turningMovements.value: 85%+ of movements meeting flow criterion 1 and 85%+ with GEH < 5; practitioners also aim for GEH < 10 on all movements

journeyTimes.value: modeled times within 15% of surveyed (or 1 minute, if higher) on more than 85% of routes

tripMatrix.value: assigned vs observed < 15% across screenline/boarding/alighting/service groups, for all or nearly all (95%) screenlines

rows.aggregation: Grouped services by corridor (onboard, entry/exit counts)
Grouped stops/stations by fare stage or corridor

assignment.lowCounts: counts under 150 passengers/hour are reported, but the criteria are not applied to them

annualPatronage.value: differences in total patronage 'as small as possible (for instance less than 5% for services with significant patronage)'

ptJourneyTimes.value: modeled within 25% of timetable times on more than 85% of routes

generalisedCostWeights.value: walk/access/egress/transfer time 1.5-2.0; waiting time 1.5-2.5; IVT rail 1, bus 1-1.4, tram/LRT 0.7-1.1; boarding/transfer penalty 2-10 minutes

convergence.value: passenger-km per service: less than 1% change between iterations for 95% of services

elasticities.range: APTA 1991 study of 52 bus systems: mean -0.40 ±0.18 SD, range -0.12 to -0.85
elasticities.source: tcrp95c12 Traveler Response Summary p. 12-6; 'Transit by Mode' pp. 12-10 to 12-11

elasticities.context: about half the bus elasticity in the same cities. BART's value is about twice that of other HRT systems (parallel freeways and express buses)
elasticities.source: tcrp95c12 p. 12-6; pp. 12-11 to 12-12 (text accompanying Table 12-3)

elasticities.value: similar to HRT; Metro-North planning values -0.15 commuters, -0.30 non-commuters (overall -0.20)

Y = 0.80 + 0.30X (% ridership loss for % fare increase X). Equals a midpoint arc elasticity of -0.39 to -0.41 for 10-40% fare changes. The common rule of thumb '10% fare rise loses 3% of riders' is a simplification of it
most commonly -0.1 to -0.6; US average excluding HRT cities about -0.4
-0.35 for city population under 500,000; -0.24 for central city over 1 million. APTA bus-only: -0.43 ±0.19 (under 1M) vs -0.36 ±0.15 (over 1M)
off-peak ridership is roughly twice as sensitive to fare changes as peak ridership
UK bus -0.2 to -0.3 short-run, -0.4 to -0.6 long-run; international bus -0.28 short-run, -0.55 long-run
elasticities.context: TCRP's own values are short-run (1-2 years)

elasticities.value: practically all observed fare elasticities lie between 0 and -1.0 (inelastic)

elasticities.range: recent observations cluster around +0.3 (mostly central-city systems) or +1.0 (suburban systems with comprehensive expansions)
elasticities.source: tcrp95c9 Traveler Response Summary pp. 9-4 to 9-5

elasticities.context: more sensitive where prior service was infrequent

elasticities.change: Bus headway, by time of day

elasticities.value: averages slightly above +0.5
peak +0.3; off-peak +0.7
typically +0.6 to +1.0 (as low as +0.3 and over +1.0 both 'not uncommon'); average +0.7 to +0.8; frequency-only changes average +0.5; with new express operation +0.9
OVT at least about 2× IVT. Newer models split between about 2× and about 4×. Over 50 US work models: wait time averages 2.12× IVT (2.72 for areas under 750,000; about 2.0 for larger cities)
elasticities.source: tcrp95c9 'Wait and Transfer Time Savings' pp. 9-21 to 9-22

elasticities.change: Out-of-vehicle vs in-vehicle time (bus routing chapter)
elasticities.value: most models 1.5 to 2.3 × IVT (Schultz 1991); Boston transfer penalty 12-15 IVT-minutes per transfer trip
about one-third to one-half of the wage rate
1 in 2 or 3 new riders from frequency improvements (and from fare cuts) would otherwise have driven

realismTestsUK.measure: elasticity of PT trips, over periods longer than a year
realismTestsUK.value: -0.2 to -0.9 (TRL 2004); values near -0.2 are unlikely for the whole market

realismTestsUK.change: London Underground fare (closest analogue to an urban metro)

realismTestsUK.value: peak elasticities < inter-peak < off-peak; non-discretionary purposes < discretionary; car-available segments > non-car-available
e = (ln T1 - ln T0)/(ln C1 - ln C0), using a 10% (or 20%) change and a converged base-year run; PT measured in person trips

total 0% (1,533,628 vs 1,529,335); local +6%, LRT -2%, heavy rail -7%, express -7%, commuter rail -49%

notFound: The original FDOT FSUTMS-Cube Framework Phase II validation standards report: fsutmsonline.net returns 404 or an HTML page. Its tables are taken from the Tennessee 2016 reprint (other.floridaFsutms2008) and FHWA Table 9.9.
Ohio and Oregon %RMSE-by-volume curves: they appear only as a chart (FHWA Figure 9.8); no tabular values were obtained.

Numeric values of FHWA Figure 9.9 (screenline maximum desirable deviation curve) and Caltrans 1992 Figure 3-9 (link maximum desirable deviation): both are graphics. The FHWA-1990 desirable link deviation by AADT is tabulated in tn2016 Table 6.
Caltrans 2014 'Travel Forecasting Guidelines': not found. Caltrans PI-0170 (2019) says the last Caltrans travel forecasting guidance was November 1992.

SF-CHAMP 5/6/7 base-year validation reports (Muni line-level R², %RMSE): not public. sfcta.org/sf-champ-modeling links only the 2002 documentation. The github.com/sfcta/sfchampdocs validation page is an empty stub. github.com/sfcta/validation_workbook holds 2023 validation scripts (Muni line, BART station, screenline, NTD operator totals) but no results. archive.sfcta.org failed the TLS handshake. UPDATE 2026-10-05: SF-CHAMP 3 (2000) and 4.1 (2008/2012) validation tables were found in Van Ness BRT and Geary BRT EIR/EIS appendices; see benchmarks.json.

MTC Travel Model One v0.5/v0.6 2010 and 2015 transit validation: published only as Tableau dashboards (modeling-website wiki), not extractable. TM1.5.2 (2015) tables were used instead. MTC Travel Model Two 2015 validation report (transit by line, R², %RMSE): not found in BayAreaMetro repos or wiki. TAMDM (TM2-based) operator totals are the only published TM2 numbers found.
Per-operator transit validation in TM1.6.1 (2023): figures only.

TCRP 95 Table 12-3 (bus vs HRT fare elasticities by city, including BART), Tables 12-5, 12-7 and 12-8 row values: the table cells lost their row labels in text extraction, so only values stated in the narrative are recorded.
